cards.text: Saul, king of Israel, wants David dead (1 Samuel 19:1). That's David, the young man the prophet Samuel anointed to be king (1 Samuel 16:1, 13). So David runs from Naioth in Ramah straight to Jonathan, SAUL'S OWN SON.

cards.question: True or false: David tells Jonathan he knows exactly what he did to make Saul want to kill him.

cards.text: Jonathan shuts that down FAST: “Far from it!” And friend, he's got a reason he's so sure.

cards.question: Why is Jonathan so sure his father isn't planning to kill David?

answers.text: His father tells him everything great or small
His father has already forgiven David
His father needs David to lead the army

cards.text: David swears, “As surely as the LORD lives and as you yourself live, there is but a step between me and death.” You know when you're copied on every email at work, and then you find out about the one meeting NOBODY invited you to? David says this is that meeting.

cards.question: David says Saul knows Jonathan favors David, so Saul keeps his plan quiet so Jonathan won't be ___.

cards.text: Then Jonathan says, “Whatever you desire, I will do for you.” So David lays out a plan: tomorrow is the New Moon, and he's supposed to dine with the king.

cards.question: Instead of dining with the king at the New Moon, David will ___ in the field until the third evening.

cards.text: If Saul misses him at all, Jonathan is to say David urgently asked to hurry to Bethlehem, his hometown. There's a yearly sacrifice there for his whole clan.

cards.question: If Jonathan tells Saul that David went to Bethlehem and Saul says good, David is safe. But if Saul is enraged, what will that tell Jonathan?

answers.text: That his father has evil intentions
That his father just needs more time
That his father feels insulted by David

cards.text: David calls himself Jonathan's servant and asks Jonathan to show him kindness. After all, Jonathan brought him into a covenant before the LORD.

cards.question: True or false: David says that if there's iniquity in him, Jonathan should kill him himself instead of bringing him to Saul.

cards.text: “Never!” Jonathan replies, and of course he'd tell David. Then David asks the real question: “Who will tell me if your father answers you harshly?”
“Come,” Jonathan replies, “let us go out to the field.” Out there, he swears by the LORD, the God of Israel, that he'll sound out his father by this time tomorrow or the next day.

cards.question: True or false: Jonathan says that if his father is favorable toward David, he'll send for David and tell him.
What does Jonathan swear he'll do if his father means to bring evil on David?

answers.text: Tell David and send him away safely
Bring David to plead with the king
Stand guard over David's hiding place

cards.text: Then Jonathan says, “May the LORD be with you, just as He has been with my father.” And he asks David to treat him with the LORD's loving devotion as long as he lives.

cards.question: Jonathan has one more request. True or false: Jonathan asks David never to cut off his loving devotion from Jonathan's household, not even when the LORD cuts off every one of David's enemies.

cards.text: So Jonathan makes a covenant with the house of David. And then he has David reaffirm his vow.

cards.question: Why does Jonathan have David reaffirm his vow?

answers.text: Out of fear of his father

cards.text: Jonathan isn't done planning. Tomorrow is the New Moon, and David's seat will be empty, so he WILL be missed.

cards.question: After three days, David is to hurry down to the place he hid when this trouble began. What should he wait beside?

cards.text: Jonathan will shoot three arrows to the side of the stone, as if aiming at a target, then send a boy to find them. Friend, this man is about to send a text message with ARROWS.

cards.question: If Jonathan tells the boy, “Look, the arrows are on this side of you; bring them,” that means it's ___ for David to come.
True or false: If Jonathan tells the boy the arrows are beyond him, David must go, because the LORD has sent him away.

cards.text: Jonathan seals it: the LORD is a witness between them forever. So David hides in the field, and the New Moon comes.

Saul sits in his usual seat by the wall, across from Jonathan and beside Abner, the commander of his army (1 Samuel 14:50). But David's seat is EMPTY, and nothing at a dinner table talks louder than an empty chair.

cards.question: On that first day, Saul says nothing about David's empty seat. What does Saul think happened to David?

answers.text: Something made him too sick to come
Something called him back to Ramah

cards.text: Day two, and David's seat is STILL empty, so Saul asks Jonathan why the son of Jesse hasn't come to the meal. That's David, Jesse's son (1 Samuel 17:12), and notice Saul doesn't say his name.

cards.question: True or false: Jonathan tells Saul that David asked permission to go to his clan's sacrifice in Bethlehem.

cards.text: Then Saul's anger burns against Jonathan. He insults Jonathan's mother and says Jonathan has chosen the son of Jesse to his own shame.

cards.question: Saul tells Jonathan that as long as the son of Jesse lives, neither Jonathan nor his ___ will be established.

cards.text: Then Saul orders him, “Now send for him and bring him to me, for he must surely die!”

cards.question: True or false: When Saul orders Jonathan to bring David to him, Jonathan agrees to do it.
Jonathan asks his father why David must be put to death and what he has done. What does Saul do next?

answers.text: He hurls his spear at Jonathan
He orders guards to seize Jonathan
He storms away from the table

cards.text: Now Jonathan knows his father is determined to kill David. He gets up from the table in fierce anger and doesn't eat any food that second day of the month.

cards.question: Why does Jonathan eat no food on the second day of the month, after leaving his father's table?

answers.text: He's hurt by how his father treated David
He's too afraid to stay near his father
He's ashamed of covering for David

cards.text: Next morning, Jonathan goes out to the field for his appointment with David, and a small boy comes with him. Jonathan tells the boy, “Run and find the arrows I shoot.”

cards.question: Saul is determined to kill David, and Jonathan's arrows are the signal for David. As the boy runs, where does Jonathan's arrow land?

answers.text: On this side of the boy

cards.text: Then Jonathan cries out, “Hurry! Make haste! Do not delay!” Three ways to say GO, which is exactly me when the timer goes off and my cookies are still in the oven.

cards.question: The boy picks up the arrow and brings it back to Jonathan. True or false: the boy knows all about the arrangement between Jonathan and David.

cards.text: Jonathan hands the boy his gear and sends him back to the city. Then David gets up from the south side of the stone, falls facedown and bows three times.

cards.question: David and Jonathan kiss each other and ___ together, though David does it more.
Before David leaves, what does Jonathan tell him?

answers.text: Go in peace because of the oath they swore
Stay hidden here until the danger passes
Come back to the king's table very soon

cards.text: Then David gets up and leaves, and Jonathan goes back into the city. Two friends, two different roads, and friend, neither road ends here.
